title: Hydraulic requirements for horizontal machine-tool slide
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Port-level open-circuit fixed-displacement hydraulic topology for one horizontal machine-tool slide axis, repaired to retain the coherent hydraulic paths while documenting the blocking research/topology gap for the exact automatic no-stop rapid-to-load-independent-feed transition. Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and DCV.P. ReliefValve.T and DCV.T return directly to Tank.R. The tandem-center 4/3 DCV provides extend, neutral unloading, and retract states. During approach extension, DCV.A supplies Cylinder.Cap through ApproachFlowControl and the proposed open PositionBypass branch, so the rapid approach path remains cap-side non-compensated meter-in controlled before the feed bypass split. At the 250 mm trip point, the proposed PositionBypass closure would force continued cap-side supply through FeedFlowControl for pressure-compensated cutting-feed meter-in. During retract, DCV.B supplies Cylinder.Rod through ReturnFlowControl for rod-side non-compensated meter-in return; cap-end exhaust returns through the one-way flow controls' internal free-reverse paths toward DCV.A and then DCV.T. This remains the closest catalog-expressible topology, but the exact position-operated bypass around a cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated feed branch is recorded as a blocking topology/research gap rather than declared validated.

motion_control_decisions.justification: Horizontal resistive extension with a specified approach time; meter-in cap-side supply control is suitable for non-overrunning motion.
Cutting feed is horizontal and resistive, but feed speed must remain materially unchanged under ±15% cutting-load variation, requiring load-independent metered supply flow.
Horizontal resistive retraction with maximum return time; meter-in rod-side supply control is suitable for non-overrunning motion.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank provides suction source and common return sink. Pump draws from Tank.S and supplies Pump.P. Pump.P branches directly to DCV.P and ReliefValve.P. DCV.T and ReliefValve.T return directly to Tank.R.
ReliefValve connects the pump pressure branch to Tank.R when relieving; set value is deferred to sizing/configuration but must be no higher than 70 bar.

Pump and Tank provide hydraulic supply and return, ReliefValve limits pressure, DCV commands cap-side pressurization for extension and rod-side pressurization for retraction, and Cylinder provides slide actuation. The metering valves provide the catalog-expressible approach, cutting-feed, proposed automatic changeover, and return flow-control functions, but the exact automatic rapid-to-load-independent-feed meter-in bypass arrangement remains a blocking topology gap.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: cap-side non-compensated meter-in approach upstream of rapid/feed split
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: In the proposed approach path, DCV.A supply passes through ApproachFlowControl before reaching the open PositionBypass and Cylinder.Cap, so the rapid approach path remains non-compensated meter-in controlled rather than unmetered.

After the proposed PositionBypass closure, FeedFlowControl meters cap-side supply in the pressure-compensated A-to-B direction during cutting feed. Load-independent feed realization depends on resolving the blocking rapid/feed bypass topology gap so no parallel feed bypass remains open during cutting feed.

PositionBypass is proposed to be open before 250 mm and closed at the trip point so continued extension is forced through FeedFlowControl without stopping or requiring a DCV shift. This is catalog-expressible but not research-validated for the exact cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated arrangement, so it is a blocking gap rather than a released valid implementation.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: rod-side non-compensated meter-in return with cap-side free reverse exhaust
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: In retract, DCV.B supply passes through ReturnFlowControl before entering Cylinder.Rod. Cap-end exhaust returns toward DCV.A through FeedFlowControl and ApproachFlowControl internal free-reverse paths.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: external machine-control command to solenoid-operated DCV
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: The hydraulic topology provides the DCV retract state and return flow path. Completion of the cutting stroke is treated as an external machine-control command to the DCV solenoid interface; sensors, wiring, and controllers are outside the hydraulic topology and are not instantiated.

design_decisions.decision: Use an open-circuit fixed-displacement pump supply with direct tank suction and common tank return.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected tank and fixed-displacement pump form the simplest catalog-compatible open-circuit supply for the slide axis; sizing is deferred. No energy-efficiency requirement is stated, and the tandem-center DCV unloads P to T in neutral.

design_decisions.decision: Use the main relief valve as the topology pressure-ceiling element.
design_decisions.rationale: The relief valve is connected directly from the pump pressure branch to tank and provides the required pressure-limiting function; its set value is deferred to sizing/configuration but must not exceed 70 bar.

design_decisions.decision: Use a tandem-center 4/3 DCV for the slide cylinder.
design_decisions.rationale: The valve provides powered extension, feed continuation, powered retraction, and a neutral pump-unloading state with blocked work ports; it is not treated as a positive safety no-creep lock.

design_decisions.decision: Place ApproachFlowControl upstream of the rapid/feed split for approach meter-in control.
design_decisions.rationale: The approach phase declares non-compensated cap-side meter-in supply control. Placing the one-way flow control upstream of both FeedFlowControl and PositionBypass prevents the open rapid bypass from creating an unmetered cap-side supply path.

design_decisions.decision: Use cap-side pressure-compensated one-way flow control for cutting-feed meter-in, conditional on resolving the bypass gap.
design_decisions.rationale: Cutting feed must remain materially stable under ±15% cutting-load variation, so the feed branch uses a pressure-compensated metering path from A to B into the cap end, with built-in free reverse flow for cap exhaust during return. Its load-independent feed realization depends on resolving the blocking rapid/feed bypass topology gap so no parallel feed bypass remains open during cutting feed.

design_decisions.decision: Retain PositionBypass only as a catalog-expressible proposed changeover element, not as a validated supported rapid/feed topology.
design_decisions.rationale: PositionBypass is the only available selected catalog class for position-triggered hydraulic phase change and is proposed to be open before the 250 mm trip and closed after the trip. However, the supplied research supports a position-operated bypass around a meter-out flow-control pattern, not the proposed cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated branch, so this candidate records a blocking topology/research gap rather than declaring the workaround valid.

design_decisions.decision: Place ReturnFlowControl in the rod-side supply path for retract meter-in control.
design_decisions.rationale: The return phase declares non-compensated rod-side meter-in supply control. Routing DCV.B through ReturnFlowControl before Cylinder.Rod realizes that typed decision and avoids a direct unmetered rod-side supply path.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add separate reverse-direction hydraulic lines or standalone duplicate check valves.
design_decisions.rationale: A physical hydraulic line is represented once, and reverse flow is provided by the selected one-way flow-control classes' internal free-reverse paths. No independent check function is required by the selected plan.

design_decisions.decision: Treat the end-of-cut return initiation as an external machine-control command, not as an added hydraulic topology component.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected solenoid DCV has a retract state and the hydraulic return path is present. Sensors, electrical wiring, controllers, and command logic are outside the hydraulic topology and are not instantiated as hydraulic components.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add pilot check, counterbalance, sensor, pressure switch, manifold, filter, gauge, wiring, motor, or accessory components.
design_decisions.rationale: The slide is horizontal/resistive and no holding or non-hydraulic topology requirement was stated; the builder must not insert unplanned accessories or non-hydraulic interfaces.

catalog_gaps.capability: Documented topology for position-operated bypass around a cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated feed-control branch, where open bypass gives rapid approach and automatic closure at 250 mm forces load-independent cutting feed without stopping.
catalog_gaps.needed_component_class: Supported rapid/feed meter-in pressure-compensated position-changeover subcircuit or validated catalog application of position_valve with pressure_comp_flow_control in this arrangement.
catalog_gaps.reason: Validation and the supplied research synthesis explicitly state that the available evidence supports a position-operated bypass around a meter-out flow-control pattern, not the proposed cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated branch used to satisfy the core requirement.
catalog_gaps.chosen_workaround: Retain the catalog-expressible PositionBypass plus FeedFlowControl arrangement only as a proposed topology pending supporting evidence; do not declare it valid.

assumptions: Pump displacement, cylinder bore/rod/stroke, valve flow ratings, and relief setting are deferred to sizing/configuration.
Mechanical position actuation for PositionBypass and solenoid actuation for DCV are properties of the selected generic classes and are not represented as separate components or external interfaces.

Reverse flow through ApproachFlowControl, FeedFlowControl, and ReturnFlowControl is represented by the selected one-way flow-control classes' internal free-reverse paths, not by duplicate reversed connection edges.
The slide load is horizontal/resistive, so no counterbalance or pilot-check holding valve is added.
End-of-cut return command timing is handled by machine controls outside this hydraulic topology.
open_issues: Blocking: the exact automatic no-stop meter-in pressure-compensated rapid/feed transition requires supporting evidence or a supported replacement circuit before topology release.
Cylinder bore/rod/stroke, pump displacement, valve flow capacity, and relief setting must be sized later to meet force, distance, speed, and 70 bar requirements.
The phrase 'must not materially change' feed speed should receive an acceptance tolerance in detailed requirements.
Machine controls must command the solenoid DCV from extend/feed to retract at cutting-stroke completion; sensors, wiring, and controllers are outside this hydraulic topology.
Every generic topology-class gap is blocking; non-equivalent workarounds cannot validate.

The core required sequence depends on a position-operated bypass around a cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated feed-control branch: bypass open for rapid approach, then closed at 250 mm to force uninterrupted load-independent cutting feed through the pressure-compensated valve. The supplied research only supports a documented position-valve bypass pattern around a meter-out flow-control circuit, and the proposed topology itself records this exact meter-in pressure-compensated rapid/feed arrangement as a blocking topology/catalog gap. Because this unresolved pattern is required to satisfy the automatic no-stop approach-to-cutting transition and load-independent cutting feed, the topology cannot be released as valid.

research_coverage.summary: Most base hydraulic elements are supported: open-circuit power/return with relief, double-acting cylinder with 4-way directional control, pressure-compensated meter-in feed control, and generic rapid/feed transition using a cam-operated bypass around a meter-out flow control. However, the core required topology remains unsupported: the accumulated findings do not cite a documented circuit where a position-operated bypass is placed around a cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated feed path to provide no-stop rapid approach-to-load-independent cutting feed transition. Because that gap affects multiple critical needs, the design cannot proceed safely and unambiguously.

items.rationale: Findings provide cited topology and placement guidance for reservoir, suction line/filter, pump, pressure/supply line, return line/filter, and a main relief valve connected near the pump outlet and returning excess flow to tank. Relief-valve evidence supports overpressure protection for blocked/stalled motion.

Findings cite a double-acting cylinder controlled by one 4-way directional valve, conventional A-to-cap/B-to-rod work-port hookup, extension/retraction actuation convention, and neutral-center behavior. Tandem-center neutral is supported for blocking the actuator while unloading the pump, with the cited caveat that spool leakage may allow creep and should not be treated as a positive safety lock.

The individual principles are cited: meter-in control at the cap-end supply for extension, pressure-compensated adjustable feed for load-independent cutting speed, reverse-flow check for return, and a generic rapid/feed transition using a cam-operated bypass. But the cited rapid/feed transition evidence is for a bypass around a meter-out flow control, not the required cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated feed path. Therefore the ordered multi-speed pattern with the typed meter-in decisions is not yet fully supported.

Cited technical sources support pressure-compensated variable flow-control valves with an adjustable orifice and compensator that maintain essentially constant flow despite inlet/load pressure changes, and support use in a meter-in cap-side branch for a resistive extending cylinder. This is sufficient for the load-independent feed-speed driver, independent of the unresolved rapid/feed bypass placement.

Cited evidence supports automatic fast/slow sequencing via a position/cam-operated 2-way valve bypassing a flow control, with rapid motion when open and slow feed when closed. However, that documented circuit bypasses a meter-out control. The required no-stop switch from rapid approach to pressure-compensated cap-side meter-in cutting feed, or a supported replacement circuit that preserves load-independent feed, is not documented.

Cited sources support a main relief/pressure-limiting valve near the pump outlet, set to the maximum allowed system pressure, opening above preset pressure to route excess flow to reservoir and protect the pump/system from overpressure during blocked or stalled motion. The specified 70 bar value is an application setting rather than a separate research gap.

The targeted finding explicitly states that the supplied sources do not document the proposed position-operated bypass around a cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated feed path for automatic rapid-to-feed transition without stopping, and do not provide a supported replacement circuit. Existing citations only support pressure-compensated flow-control port behavior and the separate meter-out bypass pattern.

missing_or_weak_information: Critical missing claim: a position- or cam-operated 2-way valve may be connected in parallel with a cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated flow-control valve so that, during extension, open bypass gives rapid approach and automatic closure at the set position forces flow through the pressure-compensated meter-in valve for load-independent cutting feed without stopping.

Critical missing alternative: a documented hydraulic circuit that achieves rapid extension over a preset distance, automatic position-based transition to adjustable pressure-compensated feed extension, and rapid retraction, while preserving the required cap-side meter-in feed decision or clearly replacing it with an equally supported load-independent topology.
The existing rapid/feed citation supports a bypass around a meter-out flow control, so it cannot by itself validate the proposed cap-side meter-in pressure-compensated bypass arrangement.
